_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.f7:CB5E: level bank: dat_FD63[(level&3)>>1] = 6,5; map page $80 or $A0 by ram_0050
comments.f7:CB79: 21 pages of map, copied as stored (no unpacking)
comments.f7:CC5B: play bank = level bank - 2 (sprites, object lists, sound tables)
comments.f7:D77D: the bank's own number is its byte at $BFFF: saved for the restore
comments.f7:D79A: spin inside the NMI until the next DLI clears ram_0047
comments.f7:DF7D: rotate the byte right twice (one 160A pixel), in each of the 8 line pages
comments.f7:E7E6: both cells of the brick become $FD (floor); score delta to $7FFB
comments.f7:FCB2: a byte = two 4-bit samples, high nibble first, one every 3 lines
